design: wild field weather stratification plus bird exclusion
key_result: cloudy/rainy weather reduced honeybee visitation; excluding birds reduced fruit/seed set by about 64%
claim_ceiling: same wild taxon two-link/near-chain evidence; weather is not randomized and no sensory-state manipulation

design: experience-controlled choice between two cultivated red varieties
key_result: UV-reflecting red Camellia received 42/57 reported first choices across bouts versus 15/57 UV-; published P=0.013
claim_ceiling: 57 choices arise from repeated bouts by 16 bees; cultivar contrast is behavioural rather than fitness and does not isolate historical selection

design: paired same-human-red species choice plus spectra
key_result: C. rusticana received about 23.45-fold more bumblebee visits than C. japonica while UV/fluorescence/bee-contrast traits differed
claim_ceiling: paired species contrast cannot isolate one sensory component and is not reproductive fitness

key_result: Apis mellifera and A. cerana preferred Deyou 2; nectar toxic-sugar composition differed among cultivars
claim_ceiling: variety association/context; no direct floral-signal manipulation and no fruit/seed fitness endpoint in this report

key_result: winter nectar volume 453.66 vs 129.14 uL and sucrose/(fructose+glucose) 49.69 vs 6.99; bird visitation, fruit set and seed set were significantly higher in winter in both populations
claim_ceiling: strong same-study observational mediation bridge; season/environment and nectar traits co-vary; no flower-colour or spectral-state contrast

design: cultivar/wild comparison plus field chlorogenic-acid fluorescence enhancement
key_result: six cultivars showed stronger blue petal fluorescence than wild plants; experimentally enhancing fluorescence increased pollinator visits (reported P<0.05)
claim_ceiling: preprint only as of 2026-09-03; no fruit/seed fitness endpoint; do not promote to primary evidence

design: breeding-mediated trait comparison across oil-tea Camellia
key_result: anthesis and flower size changes altered native-pollinator interaction; pollen-transfer efficiency contributed more to fruit set than attractiveness
claim_ceiling: preprint only as of 2026-09-03; morphology/phenology rather than colour/spectral state; do not promote to primary evidence
